_comment: Licence allow-list for the FRONTEND's production npm dependencies.
Enforced by `npm run check:licenses` in events-frontend (scripts/check-licenses.mjs).
This is the npm half of one policy. The JVM half is config/allowed-licenses-jvm.json, checked
by `./gradlew checkLicense`. They are separate files because the two ecosystems speak
different vocabularies — npm reports SPDX identifiers ('BSD-2-Clause'), while the Gradle
plugin reports its normaliser's prose names ('The 2-Clause BSD License'). Same policy, two
SCOPE — `dependencies`, not `devDependencies`. Build and test tooling never reaches a user.
Note this is still broader than what is bundled and served: it is the dependency graph, so
build-time transitives such as @babel/* (via vue -> @vue/compiler-sfc) appear here.
DUAL LICENCES — a package passes if ANY of its licences is allowed, matching how the Gradle
plugin behaves. '(MIT OR CC0-1.0)' therefore passes on MIT.
TO ADD AN ENTRY — permissive, or weak copyleft used as an unmodified library. Strong copyleft
(GPL without the Classpath Exception), network copyleft (AGPL) and source-available licences
(SSPL, BUSL, Elastic-2.0) are NOT acceptable: this project ships a public network service whose
own source is Apache-2.0. Add a line to `_rationale` for anything that is not obviously
permissive, rather than adding it silently.

_rationale.BlueOak-1.0.0: Plain-language permissive licence used by the npm/glob family. No copyleft; attribution only, which the notices page provides.
_rationale.MPL-2.0: Weak copyleft, file-level. Reaches us only via lightningcss, a Tailwind v4 transitive used unmodified, so the source-disclosure obligation does not attach to our code. Prefer a permissive alternative if one appears.
_rationale.CC-BY-4.0: caniuse-lite's browser-support DATA, not code. Requires attribution, which the notices page provides. Build-time only; none of it is served.
_rationale.OFL-1.1: The SIL Open Font License, covering @fontsource-variable/geist. This one DOES ship — the font is self-hosted and served to every visitor, deliberately (see the privacy notice). OFL permits bundling and web-serving; it forbids selling the font on its own and reusing the Reserved Font Name, neither of which we come near.
